messages:
samir: FYI customer 'AtlasRetail' filed a support escalation — p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~700ms to ~1.9s around 09:10 UTC. Noticed after a deploy? Anyone else seeing this?
maya: I see the spike in the dashboard — per-route p95 stayed ~200ms, p99 jumped. Looks correlated to continuous-batcher queueing on small prompts.
liam: Logs show a lot of very short requests stacking up. continuous-batcher metrics: avg_batch_size down to 2.1, batch_wait_ms hitting configured max 45ms frequently.
anya: Could be the time-first behavior: when traffic is lots of tiny prompts, we end up waiting full max_wait for each batch, causing tail to balloon.
samir: Repro steps from customer: many concurrent tiny prompts (mean tokens ~12), concurrency ~60, steady. They didn't change model.
maya: Grabbed a trace from 09:12: `request_id=at-34ab, route=/v1/generate, wait_ms=45, batch_size=2, processing_ms=300` — so waiting then normal processing but p99 = wait_ms + processing_ms + kernel jitter.
liam: Stack snippet from runtime logs: ```
[09:12:10.123] batcher: enqueue req=at-34ab size=12
[09:12:10.168] batcher: dispatch batch_id=987 size=2 waited=45ms
[09:12:10.470] runtime: infer started batch_id=987
[09:12:10.790] runtime: infer done batch_id=987
```
anya: That matches time-first config. For tiny prompts/time-sensitive customers we should prefer size-first or reduce max_wait_ms.
samir: Can we quickly test a per-route override for AtlasRetail: set `continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms` -> 20ms and `min_batch_size` -> 4? If traffic is many tiny ones, forcing slightly larger size or lower wait might help.
liam: I can patch a canary config on prod-north with `route=atlasretail` override. Will run for 10m and watch p99.
ops-bot: support ticket created: #12345 (priority P2) — https://support.redwood.example/tickets/12345 :white_check_mark:
support-bot: Noted customer reported impacted endpoints: `/v1/generate`, `/v1/chat/stream`.
maya: Quick simulation on staging: synthetic traffic of 60 c/s, token payload ~12, with `max_wait_ms=45` p99=1.8s; with `max_wait_ms=20` p99 drops to ~800ms but p95 increases slightly. Tradeoff visible.
liam: Canary applied at 09:28: `continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms=20` `min_batch_size=3` for route atlasretail (prod-north). Monitoring now.
anya: Also consider enabling `small_request_bypass=true` for that route so ultra-small payloads go through fast-path (no batching). Might increase cost but improves latency.
samir: Customer response: "saw improvement — tail looks better but occasional 1.1s spikes remain".
maya: Looking at traces post-canary: batch_wait mostly ~18-22ms, batch_size bumped to ~3. processing still ~300ms, p99 ~950ms. Improvement but not perfect.
liam: Next mitigation: implement adaptive wait reduction — if avg_batch_size < 3 for N windows, set max_wait_ms = max(10, current/2). Could be a short-term policy.
anya: Agree. Ops action: 1) Keep canary for 30m. 2) Add per-route small_request_bypass flag as an option. 3) Postmortem to capture config defaults and recommended profiles.
samir: Also add a note to docs: "For high concurrencies of tiny prompts, prefer size-first batching or <=20ms wait; enable bypass for latency-sensitive customers".
ops-bot: Canary metrics summary @09:40 — p99 down 48%, p95 +12% (expected), QPS steady.
liam: Rolling the per-route override to all atlasretail nodes in prod-north at 09:45.
maya: Filing a quick incident note in #incidents with links to traces and the support ticket.
anya: Follow-up: long-term, we should expose continuous-batcher policies in console per-route with presets: latency-sensitive, cost-optimized, balanced.
samir: Thanks team. I'll reply to customer with the mitigations and ETA for follow-up.
liam: For the record, config we tested: `{"max_wait_ms":20,"min_batch_size":3,"small_request_bypass":false}` then `bypass=true` gave best latency.
maya: Marking this thread as resolved for the immediate P2. We'll keep an eye. :thumbsup:
